title: Why are domain registrations growing so fast in 2026?
summary: Registered domains grew 8.7% in a year to 411.6 million, after 1.2% to 2.6% a year from 2022 to 2024. Here is what Verisign says is driving it, AI included.
body_markdown:
Registered domains grew **8.7%** in the year to September 30, 2026, to 411.6 million, according to Verisign’s[Domain Name Industry Brief](https://www.dnib.com/articles/the-domain-name-industry-brief-q3-2026) of October 22, 2026. From 2022 to 2024 they grew between 1.2% and 2.6% a year. Verisign says registrar marketing, new businesses and AI tools that make website creation easier are driving record new .com and .net registrations.


## How fast are domain registrations growing?


Verisign counts the registered domains in every extension, generic and country-code, each quarter. There were 350.4 million at the end of 2022, 359.8 million at the end of 2023 and 364.3 million at the end of 2024. Then it sped up. The total reached 386.9 million at the end of 2025 and 411.6 million on September 30, 2026, **33 million** more than a year earlier.


The speed-up shows quarter by quarter. Growth compared with a year earlier was 1.7% in the first quarter of 2025 and has risen in every quarter since, to 8.1% in the second quarter of 2026 and 8.7% in the third. In the third quarter of 2026 alone, the total grew by 10.0 million, or 2.5%.


Not every group of extensions grew at that pace. .com and .net together reached 182.5 million at the end of September 2026, up 6.1% in a year. Country-code extensions such as .de and .uk reached 151.4 million, up 4.6%. Both grew more slowly than the total, so the remaining extensions, which include .org, .info and newer ones such as .xyz and .shop, grew faster as a group.


Our own count from registry zone files, which covers fewer extensions than Verisign’s, shows the same direction for .com. Its zone-file count rose 6.8% in the 12 months to October 31, 2026, from 157.7 million to 168.5 million. The two counts are measured differently, so we never add them together.


## What is driving the growth?


Verisign runs the .com and .net registries. It processed **13.1 million** new .com and .net registrations in the third quarter of 2026, up from 10.6 million a year earlier, according to its[third-quarter results](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1014473/000101447326000038/q32026earningsrelease.htm) of October 22, 2026. On the[earnings call](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/22/verisign-vrsn-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/) that day, chief executive Jim Bidzos called it “a record 13.1 million new registrations processed during the third quarter”.


In his prepared remarks, Bidzos said: “Registrars have successfully engaged with our marketing programs and are focused on customer acquisition, plus AI tools are making content and website creation faster and easier.”


Quarter New .com and .net registrations Source


Third quarter of 2025 10.6 million Verisign results, October 22, 2026


Second quarter of 2026 12.7 million Verisign earnings call, October 22, 2026


Third quarter of 2026 13.1 million Verisign results, October 22, 2026


Asked about demand later in the call, he described “a synergistic convergence of demand for domain names from businesses, new business starts, but also our marketing programs and, an AI tailwind”. That gives three drivers in Verisign’s own words:


- Registrar marketing, with registrars using Verisign’s marketing programs and focusing on new customers.
- Demand from businesses, including new business starts.
- AI tools that make content and website creation faster and easier.


Verisign does not say how much of the growth each driver explains.


## Is AI really creating more domains?


The evidence that AI plays a part comes from Verisign. On the call, Bidzos said “we are hearing from some registrars that AI is a factor. AI, clearly makes it easier to find a domain name, develop a website, and maintain a website.”


Verisign’s[quarterly report to the SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1014473/000101447326000039/vrsn-20260930.htm) for the same quarter gives the same reasons. It says growth “has been positively impacted by continued registrar focus on customer acquisition and engagement with our marketing programs, as well as the evolution of AI tools used in content and website creation.”


What the evidence does not show is how many new domains exist because of AI. Verisign names AI next to marketing and new businesses, gives no split, and does not report why each domain was registered. So AI is one of several drivers Verisign names, not a measured cause.


AI also shows up in what buyers pay for names. On[DNJournal’s 2026 year-to-date sales chart](https://dnjournal.com/ytd-sales-charts.htm) , checked on November 18, 2026, **39 of the 112** entries are .ai domains. The top .ai sale is Bot.ai at $1,200,000, sold through Sedo. The second-largest entry is AI.com at $70,000,000, which DNJournal notes closed in 2025.

## Are domain prices going up?


Yes, for .com and .net. The .com wholesale price, which registrars pay Verisign, rose **7%** on November 1, 2026, from $10.26 to $10.97, as Verisign[announced](https://investor.verisign.com/news-releases/news-release-details/verisign-reports-first-quarter-2026-results/) on April 23, 2026. Verisign is allowed to raise it by up to 7% a year through 2029, but it has not announced any later increase. The .net wholesale price rises from $10.91 to $12.00 on March 1, 2027.


Registrars set their own prices on top of the wholesale price, so the price you pay is usually higher. Our guide to[what a domain name costs](https://instantdomainsearch.com/learn/guides/how-much-does-a-domain-name-cost) explains the rest.

## What this means if you are naming something


With more names registered every quarter, check the name you want before you build around it. A[domain search](https://instantdomainsearch.com/) shows which extensions are free as you type, and the[domain generator](https://instantdomainsearch.com/domain-generator) suggests available variations when yours is taken. The[business name generator](https://instantdomainsearch.com/business-name-generator) helps if you still need a name.


If the name is taken,[expired domains](https://instantdomainsearch.com/expired-domains) lists names that owners let go, and[domain appraisal](https://instantdomainsearch.com/domain-appraisal) estimates what a name is worth before you make an offer. Compare renewal prices as well as first-year prices, because the .com price can rise each year through 2029.


The monthly[State of Domains](https://instantdomainsearch.com/trends) report ranks the fastest-growing extensions.[Domain name statistics](https://instantdomainsearch.com/domain-extensions/statistics) charts the largest extensions month by month since 2016, and[Domain Extensions](https://instantdomainsearch.com/domain-extensions) lists every one you can search.


## Frequently asked questions


### How many domain names are registered in 2026?


There were 411.6 million at the end of September 2026, according to Verisign’s brief of October 22, 2026. Our guide to[how many domains there are](https://instantdomainsearch.com/learn/guides/how-many-domains-are-there) breaks it down by extension.


### Why are domain registrations increasing?


Verisign names registrar marketing, new businesses and AI tools that make website creation easier, but not how much each one adds.


### Is AI causing more domain registrations?


AI is one of several factors. On October 22, 2026, Verisign said some registrars call AI a factor, but no source measures its share.


### How many new .com domains are registered each quarter?


Verisign processed 13.1 million new .com and .net registrations in the third quarter of 2026, up from 10.6 million a year earlier, and reports the two together.


### Are .com prices going up?


Yes. The .com wholesale price rose 7% to $10.97 on November 1, 2026, and it can rise by up to 7% a year through 2029.

Verisign’s[methodology](https://www.dnib.com/methodology) leaves out .tk, .cf, .ga, .gq and .ml, and its figures are estimates that can change as more complete data arrives. Its total includes country-code extensions that don’t publish zone files. Our own figures come from registry zone files, which cover fewer extensions, so the two totals differ. Our guide to[how many domains there are](https://instantdomainsearch.com/learn/guides/how-many-domains-are-there) explains the difference and lists the count by extension.
